title: Cong Wei (@CongWei1230) — thread (6 tweets)
summary:
[1/6] 🚀 Introduce UniIR, a unified instruction-guided multimodal retriever handles diverse tasks.
- 1️⃣model for 8️⃣ retrieval tasks (SoTA w/ Instruction-tuning)
- Generalizes to unseen retrieval tasks.
- M-BEIR: multimodal retrieval benchmark w/ 10 datasets, 1.1M queries, 5.6M cands.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GANEm2nWwAAlJIu.jpg
────────
[2/6] (2/6) Unlike traditional IR systems, the UniIR(Universal multimodal Information Retrieval) model needs to follow the instructions to process a heterogeneous query and retrieve information from a heterogeneous candidate pool🌐 with millions of candidates in diverse modalities.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GANFquGWUAAsxlT.jpg
────────
[3/6] (4/6) Zero-shot vision language pre-trained models struggle to retrieve queried information from M-BEIR’s heterogeneous pool. But UniIR achieves SOTA on multiple tasks with instruction-tuning.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GANF5NDXEAAoJ-c.jpg
────────
[4/6] (3/6) To train and evaluate UniIR, we build a large-scale retrieval benchmark📊named M-BEIR (Multimodal BEnchmark for Instructed Retrieval). The M-BEIR benchmark comprises 8 retrieval tasks and 10 datasets, encompassing 1.1 M queries and a heterogeneous pool of 5.6 M candidates.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GANFyubXsAApfzG.jpg
────────
[5/6] (5/6) Excited to see UniIR show zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks! During training, we excluded three datasets (WebQA, OVEN, CIRR) to fine-tune UniIR on other M-BEIR datasets. At test time, UniIR showed remarkable zero-shot performance on these held-out datasets!
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GANGIhvXUAE5rSB.jpg
────────
[6/6] (6/6)

title: Cong Wei (@CongWei1230) — thread (5 tweets)
summary:
[1/5] 🚀 Meet AnyV2V, a plug-and-play framework for any video-to-video editing tasks.
- AnyV2V disentangles the video editing process into1️⃣first-frame editing and2️⃣I2V generation (via DDIM inversion & feature injection)
- AnyV2V can plug in any existing image editing and I2V model 🖼
🎬 https://pbs.twimg.com/ext_tw_video_thumb/1771527309545156608/pu/img/_kRWn6iXOlg3Xv9-.jpg | https://video-s.twimg.com/ext_tw_video/1771527309545156608/pu/vid/avc1/360x270/Ne7KwUE5pkJmJ9Dp.mp4?tag=12
────────
[2/5] (2/7) In the 1st stage, AnyV2V applies an image editing method on the first frame. In the 2nd stage, the source video is DDIM inverted to an initial noise. An I2V model generates the edited video condition on the edited 1st frame with feature and attention injection in the U-Net.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GJW6yEuWIAASVin.jpg
────────
[3/5] (3/7) Prompt-based Editing. By leveraging the strength of image editing models, the AnyV2V framework offers precise editing, altering only targeted elements while keeping the rest of the scene intact. The baseline methods display either excessive or insufficient changes.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GJW62bCXQAEpOiQ.jpg
────────
[4/5] (5/7) Subject-driven Editing. Given one subject image, AnyDoor-equipped AnyV2V replaces an object in the video with the target subject while maintaining the video motion and persevering the background.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GJW692lXgAEe--9.jpg
────────
[5/5] (7/7)

title: Cong Wei (@CongWei1230)
summary:
Thrilled to present my recent work: OmniEdit! Using 7 specialists + cost-efficient InternVL2-8B judge （scoring ability distilled from GPT-4o), we curated 1.2M **high-res** (~1 MP) editing pairs across **various aspect ratios**:
Quoting @WenhuChen
I'm super excited to share our recent work OmniEdit, an omnipotent editing model to handle all different types of editing requests including addition, removal, swapping, environment, background, style, etc. The best part is the **highest-quality** 1.2M high-resolution image editing dataset in
The biggest blocker in image editing is the lack of high-quality editing pairs. Most existing released datasets are highly noisy, low-resolution, with strong artifacts. This basically prohibits the progress in this area.
We spent **8 months** to experiment with many approaches to synthesize and filter clean image editing pairs. Eventually, we built seven specialized pipelines to propose massive amount of candidates and then prompt GPT-4o to assign quality scores these candidates. We took the highest-ranked candidates as our 1.2M training data.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/Gd_up4zXYAAzeSq.jpg

title: Cong Wei (@CongWei1230) — thread (6 tweets)
summary:
[1/6] 🚀Thrilled to introduce ☕️MoCha: Towards Movie-Grade Talking Character Synthesis
Please unmute to hear the demo audio.
✨We defined a novel task: Talking Characters, which aims to generate character animations directly from Natural Language and Speech input.
✨We propose MoCha, the first-of-its-kind DiT model capable of achieving movie-grade talking character generation.
✨MoCha enables, for the first time, Multi-character Conversations with Turn-based Dialogue generation, pushing the boundaries of automated filmmaking.
Paper:
Project website:
🎬 https://pbs.twimg.com/ext_tw_video_thumb/1906876438386503680/pu/img/Wzv7WAr7J2AiVl1K.jpg | https://video-s.twimg.com/ext_tw_video/1906876438386503680/pu/vid/avc1/498x270/mkdJi5oX4TUijqqR.mp4?tag=12
────────
[2/6] Speech-Video Window Attention
We propose a novel attention mechanism that aligns speech and video inputs through localized temporal conditioning. This design significantly improves lip-sync accuracy and speech-video alignment
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GnaWTcCXAAA6n4z.jpg
────────
[3/6] End-to-End Training Without Auxiliary Conditions.
MoCha is a DiT model that trained directly on text and speech input without any auxiliary conditioning.
MoCha projects speech, video, text all into tokens.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GnaWJ2MW8AA3j4V.jpg
────────
[4/6] Joint Speech-Text Training Strategy
To address the scarcity of large-scale speech-labeled video datasets, we introduce a joint training framework that leverages both speech-labeled and text-labeled video data. This strategy enhances the model’s ability to generalize across diverse character actions and enables universal controllability through natural language prompts, enabling nuanced control of character expressions, actions, interactions, and environments without auxiliary signals.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GnaWdxWXAAE1Mfd.jpg
────────
[5/6] Multi-Character Conversation Generation
We designed structured prompt templates with a character tagging mechanism, enabling, for the first time, multi-character conversation with turn-based dialogue.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/GnaWYLLXMAAQYCd.jpg
────────
[6/6] Heartfelt thanks to my internship mentor Bo Sun and my Phd supervisor @WenhuChen
, and our incredible collaborators @HaoyumaU, @j1h0u, @felixudr, Zecheng He, @XiaoliangDai_, Luxin Zhang, Kunpeng Li, Tingbo Hou, Animesh Sinha, and @vaphab at Meta.
Working as a research intern at Meta was both a rewarding and truly enjoyable experience!♥️

[1/4] [1/5] UniVideo consists of two core components: a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) and a Multimodal DiT (MM-DiT).
The MLLM handles vision–language understanding, taking text, image, and video as multimodal instructions.
The MM-DiT focuses on visual generation with two branches:
• one injects semantic guidance from the MLLM
• the other provides fine-grained reconstruction signals from a VAE
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G-JrkRVbMAA52VU.jpg
────────
[2/4] [2/5] To align the pretrained MLLM with the diffusion generator, we explore different architectural design choices.
We find that MMDiT with self-attention is easier to align with the MLLM than cross-attention–based DiT models.
With MMDiT, alignment only requires training a lightweight MLP connector, while keeping both the MLLM and generator fully frozen.
In contrast, cross-attention DiT models often require unfreezing the DiT, a heavy connector, or longer training cycles, making alignment more complex.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G-JsIz3a0AAavkt.jpg
────────
[3/4] [3/5] We train UniVideo jointly on diverse tasks, including in-context video generation, in-context video editing, video stylization, image editing, text-to-image, and text-to-video.
Despite this unified training, UniVideo achieves superior or competitive performance across a wide range of tasks compared to strong baselines.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G-JsjIraAAAT3Y8.jpg
────────
[4/4] [4/5] We observe two types of generalization in UniVideo, highlighting the advantages of unified modeling:
(i) Cross-domain generalization.
Although UniVideo is not trained on general free-form video editing data, it transfers editing capabilities from diverse image editing data to the video domain. Joint training with in-context video generation and limited video editing tasks (deletion, swapping, addition, stylization) enables UniVideo to handle previously unseen free-form video editing instructions.
(ii) Compositional task generalization.
UniVideo also generalizes to novel task compositions that were never seen during training—such as combining editing with style transfer within a single instruction.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G-JtZJFbgAEV-7A.jpg

title: Cong Wei (@CongWei1230) — thread (3 tweets)
summary:
[1/3] 🚀 Introducing RationalRewards — a reasoning-based reward model that improves image generation(t2i and editing) quality at both training and test time.
🧠 We taught reward models to think before they score, leading to more reliable feedback and reduced reward hacking during RL fine-tuning.
🔁 At test time, the same RationalRewards model performs prompt tuning by iteratively generating, scoring with reasoning, and rewriting prompts.
Here’s the surprising part 👇
test-time prompt tuning matches — sometimes beats — full RL fine-tuning, which costs 400 GPU hours.🔥
💡 This suggests an alternative to parameter tuning: your diffusion model may already have strong capabilities — prompt tuning matters.

title: Cong Wei (@CongWei1230)
clean_title: PixelUMM: a unified multimodal model working directly in pixel space
summary:
In this Gemini Notebook video overview, we are going to take a look at :
PixelUMM is an encoder free unified multimodal model created by NVIDIA and the University of Waterloo that handles both visual understanding and generation directly in pixel space without relying on traditional pretrained visual encoders or variational autoencoders.
The work was done by :
Cong Wei1,2 Xuanchi Ren1 Bryan Chu1 Weiming Ren2 Huan Ling1 Jiahui Huang1
Laura Leal-Taixé1 Sanja Fidler1 Wenhu Chen2 Zian Wang1 Jay Zhangjie Wu1
By representing images as spatial patches and videos as spatiotemporal tubelets connected to a Mixture of Transformers backbone via single layer linear projections, the framework jointly supports autoregressive text prediction and pixel space flow matching. The system utilizes generalized causal attention and a structured training schedule to process diverse tasks, including image and video understanding alongside text to image and text-to-video generation. Empirical analyses examine key design choices such as patch size and decoder alternatives, showing that less aggressive spatial and temporal compression improves performance while maintaining competitive results across multiple benchmarks.
🎬 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HTrAMEgbsAAd-ef.jpg | https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2106207089483993088/vid/avc1/480x270/4CiUc0C5o89IABTr.mp4?tag=29
clean_summary:
Usually, models that understand or generate images and videos rely on pretrained visual encoders or autoencoders to process visual data. This adds complexity and can limit flexibility. PixelUMM, created by NVIDIA and the University of Waterloo, skips these steps by working directly with pixels, treating images as spatial patches and videos as spatiotemporal tubelets.

PixelUMM connects these patches and tubelets to a Mixture of Transformers backbone using simple linear projections. It supports tasks like text prediction, image and video understanding, and text-to-image or text-to-video generation. By using generalized causal attention and a structured training schedule, it balances spatial and temporal compression to improve performance while staying competitive on benchmarks.

Cong Wei points to Yuxuan for details on RewardHarness and ClawBench, which were presented at COLM 2026. RewardHarness is a framework that learns human preferences for image editing using as few as 100 demonstrations by evolving a library of skills and tools.

ClawBench is a benchmark for AI browser agents, ranking them on 130 real-world tasks with a two-stage scoring system involving HTTP-request interception and an LLM judge. These tools help measure and improve AI alignment and agent performance in practical settings.

linked_urls.title: RewardHarness: Learning Human Preferences for Image Editing with Only 100 Demonstrations
linked_urls.summary: RewardHarness — a self-evolving agentic reward framework that aligns with human preferences from as few as 100 demonstrations by iteratively evolving a library of Skills and Tools.
